Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the MCAS blank-by-blank submission and the standing market-conduct exam readiness file; escalation to Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Alaska Title 21 (AS 21.06.120 examination authority, AS 21.09.200 annual reporting) read alongside the current-year NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions and the state's MCAS participation bulletin; re-read each January when NAIC publishes the data-year blank (supporting: Alabama Title 27, Arkansas Insurance Code)

In-scope processes.value: Policy issuance and cancellation/non-renewal, claims adjudication and closure, consumer complaint handling, producer appointment and termination - for every line NAIC collects MCAS on (private passenger auto, homeowners, life, annuity, long-term care, health, lender-placed, travel), in each of the 51 jurisdictions where direct written premium for that line exceeds the participation threshold

In-scope systems.value: NAIC Regulatory Data Collection (RDC) portal for MCAS entry and submission, iSite+ for regulator distribution and acceptance status; source extracts pulled from Guidewire PolicyCenter, Guidewire ClaimCenter and the complaint case log

Compliance procedure documented.value: MCAS Filing and Exam Readiness Procedure - participation determination by state and line, data-element-to-source-field mapping, extract and validation run book, Annual Statement reconciliation, interrogatory drafting, officer attestation, plus the standing Chapter 16 standardized data request (SDR) readiness file build

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Controller signing the reconciliation section; re-approved each year after the NAIC data call changes are absorbed and whenever a source system (PolicyCenter/ClaimCenter) release changes a mapped field

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Data year ends 31 December; property/casualty MCAS lines (private passenger auto, homeowners, other P&C blanks) are due 30 April and life, annuity, long-term care, health, lender-placed and travel blanks are due 30 June; internal cut-offs at 15 March (extract frozen) and 31 March (reconciliation signed) per state per line

Deadline reminders configured.value: Compliance calendar tasks per state per blank at T-90, T-45, T-15 and T-3 business days to the 30 April / 30 June RDC due dates, plus a weekly open-blank status mail to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager from 1 March until every blank shows Submitted in RDC

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submitted MCAS blanks (all states, all lines), RDC submission confirmations and confirmation numbers, validation-error clearance notes, the Annual Statement state-page reconciliation, the officer attestation, and the exam readiness file are retained 5 years from the data year end in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed blank, a late submission past 30 April/30 June, an unresolved RDC validation error, or a post-submission data restatement is logged as a market-conduct exception with the state, blank, data element, root cause and refile date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every restated or late-filed MCAS blank and every gap found in the exam readiness file before the readiness file is declared current

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every state-and-line combination with direct written premium in the data year (from the Annual Statement state pages) crossed against the blanks actually submitted in RDC, plus the underlying policy, claim and complaint record counts feeding each submitted blank

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero missed or late blanks; MCAS written premium must tie to the Annual Statement state page within 0.5% per state and line with a written explanation for any variance; any claim-count or complaint-count element differing from the source system extract by more than 1% fails

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual per state per line, so the test runs annually in the July following the data year over the full submitted population, with a mid-year (September) spot check that the exam readiness file is still current

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared, mapped or attested any sampled MCAS blank and must not report to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual MCAS and exam-readiness test workpaper - state/line population extract, RDC submission list, sample, re-performance notes, reconciliation schedules and exception log - filed in the compliance evidence repository under the data year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: MCAS submitted-blank pack per state plus the Chapter 16 SDR readiness file (policy, claim, complaint and producer registers with data dictionaries, written procedures, forms and rate manuals in force during the exam period), producible to the Alaska Division of Insurance within the 10 business days a market conduct exam data call normally allows

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance is the single point of contact for the Alaska Division of Insurance and for any NAIC MCAS data inquiry; Regulatory Counsel clears any restatement notice or admission of a missed blank before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Determine which states and lines trigger an MCAS blank this data year
actions: Ask the Controller for the prior-year Annual Statement state pages (Schedule T and the by-state direct written premium exhibits) for every writing company and NAIC co-code.

Download the current NAIC MCAS Participation Requirements table and the per-line premium threshold (USD 50,000 direct written premium in the state for the line is the standard trigger) from the NAIC MCAS page.

Build a state-by-line grid: for each of the 51 jurisdictions and each MCAS line (private passenger auto, homeowners, life, annuity, long-term care, health, lender-placed, travel), enter direct written premium and mark IN SCOPE or BELOW THRESHOLD.
For Alaska specifically, confirm the Division of Insurance is a participating MCAS state for each marked line and note the AS 21.06.120 examination authority the data supports.
Send the grid to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for confirmation and file it as the filing inventory for the data year.
checklist.done: a signed state-by-line filing inventory exists showing premium, threshold test and IN SCOPE / BELOW THRESHOLD for all 51 jurisdictions.

checklist.step: Pull the current data-year MCAS blank, definitions and interrogatories
actions: Log in to the NAIC Regulatory Data Collection (RDC) portal with the company MCAS filer account and open the data year under MCAS.
Download for each in-scope line the blank template, the Data Call and Definitions document and the interrogatory list, and save them to the data-year folder named mcas-<line>-<data year>.
Redline this year's definitions against last year's and list every added, deleted or re-worded data element on a change sheet.
Circulate the change sheet to Claims, Underwriting Operations and the Complaints Manager with the specific elements each of them sources.
Confirm the RDC filer account and the officer attestation account are both active before March, since account resets take days to clear.
checklist.done: the data-year blanks, definitions and interrogatories are downloaded, a year-over-year change sheet is issued, and RDC access is proven live.

checklist.step: Map every MCAS data element to a named source system field
actions: Create one mapping row per MCAS data element: element number, element name, NAIC definition text, source system, table, field, and the filter logic that selects the records.

Point policy elements (policies in force at year end, new business written, cancellations, non-renewals) at Guidewire PolicyCenter fields and state the state-of-risk field used for jurisdiction assignment.

Point claims elements (claims opened, closed with payment, closed without payment, and the 0-30 / 31-60 / 61-90 / 91-180 / over-180 day settlement buckets) at Guidewire ClaimCenter date fields, naming which date starts the clock (date of notice) and which ends it (final payment date).
Point complaint elements at the complaint case log and state whether the count is complaints received directly, complaints received from the Division of Insurance, or both.
Have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager review and sign the mapping before any extract runs; unsigned mappings do not go to production.
checklist.done: every element on every in-scope blank has a signed mapping row naming system, table, field and filter logic.

checklist.step: Extract and freeze the policy and underwriting population
actions: Run the MCAS policy extract for the data year against PolicyCenter as of a fixed 15 March freeze snapshot, partitioned by state of risk, line and writing company.
Produce counts for policies in force at 31 December, new business policies written during the year, cancellations by reason code, and non-renewals initiated by the company.
Exclude out-of-scope business explicitly (assumed reinsurance, non-MCAS lines, run-off companies) and record the exclusion rule and the row count removed by each rule.
Write the extract, the row counts and the query hash to the data-year folder and notify the Regulatory Reporting Analyst that the population is frozen.
Re-runs after the freeze require a written request from the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and a new version number.
checklist.done: a frozen, versioned policy extract with per-state counts and documented exclusion rules is delivered to Regulatory Reporting.

checklist.step: Extract the claims population and compute the settlement-timing buckets
actions: Run the MCAS claims extract from ClaimCenter for the data year by state of loss, line and coverage, using the 15 March freeze snapshot.

Compute for each claim the days from date of notice to final payment and assign it to the MCAS bucket (0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-180, over 180 days), leaving reopened claims flagged separately as the definitions require.
Produce claims closed with payment, closed without payment, claims open at year end, and the median and total paid amounts each blank asks for.
Hand the bucket logic to the Claims Director / Manager for confirmation that the date fields used match how adjusters actually close files.
File the extract, the bucket distribution and the confirmation mail in the data-year folder.
checklist.done: claim counts and settlement-timing buckets are produced from a frozen ClaimCenter extract with the date logic confirmed by Claims.

checklist.step: Extract the complaint population and reconcile it to the state complaint registers
actions: Export every complaint case with a received date in the data year, split into complaints received directly from consumers and complaints forwarded by a department of insurance.
Reconcile the department-forwarded count for each state to the NAIC Complaints Database Application (CDS) record and, for Alaska, to the Division of Insurance consumer complaint correspondence file.
Investigate and document any difference greater than one case per state before the count is used, since a complaint-count mismatch is the fastest way to trigger a targeted exam.
Produce complaint counts by reason code and by line to support the interrogatory answers.
Send the reconciled counts to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst with the reconciliation schedule attached.
checklist.done: complaint counts by state, line and source are reconciled to the CDS/Division records with every difference explained in writing.

checklist.step: Run the validation and reasonableness edits before anything enters RDC
actions: Run the NAIC published MCAS validation rules for each blank: internal sum checks (claims closed with payment plus closed without payment plus open must reconcile to claims opened plus prior-year open), non-negative counts, and required-if-populated pairings.
Run the year-over-year variance edit: flag any element moving more than 20% against the prior data year and require a written business explanation on the flag sheet.
Flag any state where a policy count is populated but the matching premium is zero, or vice versa.
Route each flag to the owning function (Underwriting Operations, Claims, Complaints) with a 5 business day response deadline ahead of the 31 March internal cut-off.
Close each flag as corrected data, accepted with explanation, or open exception - never silently.
checklist.done: all NAIC validation rules and the 20% variance edit are run and every flag is closed with a corrected value or a written explanation.

checklist.step: Reconcile MCAS premium to the Annual Statement state pages
actions: Take the direct written premium by state and line from the filed Annual Statement state pages and Schedule T for each writing company.
Line it up against the MCAS premium element for the same state, line and company on a reconciliation schedule.

Explain every difference by a named cause (line-of-business grouping differences between the Annual Statement line and the MCAS line, non-MCAS coverage inside a statutory line, mid-year company transfers) with the amount attributed to each cause.
Escalate any unexplained variance above 0.5% to the Controller before the blank is submitted.
Have the Controller sign the reconciliation schedule and file it with the data-year evidence, because examiners ask for this schedule first.
checklist.done: a Controller-signed schedule ties MCAS premium to the Annual Statement state pages for every state and line, with variances above 0.5% explained.

checklist.step: Draft the interrogatory answers with the business owners
actions: Take each interrogatory from the data-year blank (use of predictive models in underwriting, use of third-party claims vendors, lawsuit and arbitration counts, replacement and free-look practices on life and annuity blanks) and assign it to the function that can actually answer it.
Collect written answers from the Underwriting Director / Manager, Claims Director / Manager and Policy Admin Ops Lead, each with a supporting document reference.
Rewrite the answers to match the definition wording in the Data Call and Definitions rather than internal jargon, and keep them consistent with what the company said last data year.
Where an answer changed year over year, note why on the answer sheet so an examiner does not read the change as an inconsistency.
File the answer sheet with its supporting references in the data-year folder.
checklist.done: every interrogatory has a written, sourced answer from the owning function with year-over-year changes explained.

checklist.step: Load each blank into the NAIC RDC portal and clear all validation errors
actions: In the RDC portal open MCAS, select the data year, the line and the writing company, and upload the completed blank file for each in-scope state.
Work the portal validation report to zero blocking errors; for each warning left open, type the required explanatory comment in the portal comment field rather than leaving it blank.
Confirm the state list loaded matches the signed filing inventory exactly - a state on the inventory with no blank in RDC is a missed filing, not a rounding issue.
Print or export the pre-submission summary per state and line and compare it field by field to the reconciled workbook.
Report the load status per state daily to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager from the first load until every blank is ready to submit.
checklist.done: every in-scope blank is loaded in RDC with zero blocking validation errors and each remaining warning carries a portal comment.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer attestation and submit before the statutory due date
actions: Send the attesting officer the reconciled workbook, the Controller-signed premium reconciliation and the open-warning list at least 5 business days before the due date.
Have the officer complete the RDC attestation screen for each blank, certifying the data is complete and accurate to the best of their knowledge.
Press Submit in RDC for the property/casualty blanks on or before 30 April and for the life, annuity, long-term care, health, lender-placed and travel blanks on or before 30 June.
Capture the RDC confirmation number, submission timestamp and submitting user for every state and line onto the filing inventory.
Any blank not submitted by the due date is logged the same day as a compliance exception and escalated to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every in-scope blank is attested and submitted on or before its 30 April / 30 June due date, with the confirmation number recorded on the inventory.

checklist.step: Confirm iSite+ acceptance and distribution to each state, including Alaska
actions: Two business days after submission, reopen the RDC filing list and check each blank shows status Submitted/Accepted rather than Pending or Rejected.
For any Rejected blank, read the NAIC rejection reason, correct the file, resubmit and record the second confirmation number alongside the first.
Confirm the Alaska Division of Insurance is listed among the recipient jurisdictions for each Alaska blank so the data actually reaches the regulator through iSite+.
Export the acceptance report and attach it to the filing inventory row for each state and line.
Mark the data year closed on the compliance calendar only when every inventory row carries an acceptance.
checklist.done: every submitted blank shows an accepted status with the receiving jurisdiction confirmed, and rejections are corrected and resubmitted.

checklist.step: Build and refresh the standing market conduct exam readiness file
actions: Structure the readiness file to the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook Chapter 16 standardized data request: separate registers for new business, cancellations/non-renewals, claims paid, claims denied, complaints, producer appointments and terminations, each with a data dictionary naming every column.

Add the governing documents an examiner will ask for on day one: underwriting guidelines, claims handling procedures, complaint handling procedure, rate and rule manuals, and the policy forms in force during each period, each version-stamped with its effective and superseded dates.
Store the current-year MCAS blanks, RDC confirmations and the premium reconciliation in the same file so the MCAS answers and the exam registers cannot diverge.
Refresh the registers quarterly from the frozen data marts and record the refresh date and row counts in the file index.
Have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager confirm quarterly that the file could be handed over within 10 business days of a data call.
checklist.done: a Chapter 16-structured readiness file with data dictionaries and version-stamped procedures is refreshed quarterly and confirmed producible in 10 business days.

checklist.step: Keep the continuous registers current between filings
actions: Maintain the complaint register in near real time: every complaint gets a state, receipt date, reason code, line, resolution date and outcome within 2 business days of receipt.
Maintain the producer appointment and termination register against the licensing system, including termination-for-cause reporting dates, since examiners test these against the state records.
Run a monthly completeness check that every claim closed in the month appears in the claims register and every policy cancelled appears in the cancellation register.
Log any register gap as a data-quality issue with the owning system, an owner and a fix date rather than backfilling silently.
Report register health monthly to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager on a one-page status.
checklist.done: the complaint, claims, cancellation and producer registers are current within one month with all gaps logged and owned.

checklist.step: Retain the filing and readiness evidence for the full retention period
actions: Move the closed data-year pack (submitted blanks, RDC confirmation numbers, acceptance report, validation clearance notes, premium reconciliation, interrogatory answers, attestation) into the evidence repository under the data year.
Apply the 5-year-from-data-year-end retention label, matching the record retention period examiners work to under state market conduct authority.
Confirm the repository index makes every record retrievable by data year, state, line, writing company and RDC confirmation number.
Place a legal hold flag on the data year if a market conduct examination or Division inquiry is open, overriding the normal disposal date.
Report the archived pack to the Head of Compliance as the annual obligation close.
checklist.done: the data-year pack is archived, retention-labelled for 5 years, retrievable by state and confirmation number, and legal-held where an exam is open.

testing.step: Build the population of state-and-line MCAS obligations for the data year
actions: Independently extract direct written premium by state, line and writing company from the filed Annual Statement state pages and Schedule T rather than from the compliance inventory.
Apply the NAIC MCAS participation table and the per-line premium threshold yourself to derive the list of blanks that should exist across all 51 jurisdictions.
Pull the RDC filing list for the data year and record every blank actually submitted with its state, line, company and confirmation number.
Reconcile the two lists and mark each row Filed, Missing, or Filed-but-not-required before any sampling begins.
testing.done: an independently derived obligation population is reconciled to the RDC filing list with every row marked Filed, Missing or Filed-but-not-required.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed blanks to the source of record and prove completeness
actions: Tie the MCAS premium element on each filed blank back to the Annual Statement state page amount and recompute the variance percentage yourself.
Confirm every variance above 0.5% carries a written, cause-attributed explanation signed by the Controller.
Compare the RDC-submitted policy, claim and complaint counts to the frozen 15 March extracts and confirm no post-freeze re-run changed a submitted figure without a version note.
List any blank whose submitted figures cannot be reproduced from the frozen extract as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every filed blank ties to the Annual Statement state page and to the frozen source extract, with unreproducible figures raised as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of rows marked Missing and 100% of the Alaska rows, since Alaska is the representative jurisdiction for this obligation.
Take 20 further state-and-line rows selected at random using a recorded seed, weighted toward the states with the largest direct written premium.
Record the seed, population size, weighting rule and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Confirm the sample covers at least one property/casualty blank (30 April deadline) and one life/annuity/health blank (30 June deadline).
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all Missing rows, all Alaska rows and both deadline cycles is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the participation and threshold determination in the sample
actions: For each sampled state and line, read the current NAIC MCAS participation requirements and the state's own MCAS bulletin without first looking at the compliance grid.
Recompute the direct written premium tested against the threshold from the Annual Statement figure and reach your own IN SCOPE / BELOW THRESHOLD conclusion.
Compare to the recorded determination; a right conclusion supported by the wrong premium figure or a stale participation list still counts as an exception.
Capture the participation page and the premium figure you relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state and line has an independent scope conclusion with the source page and premium figure captured.

testing.step: Re-derive the key data elements from the source systems
actions: For each sampled blank, re-run the claims settlement-timing calculation from ClaimCenter data: days from date of notice to final payment, bucketed 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-180 and over 180 days.
Re-run the policies-in-force-at-year-end and cancellation counts from PolicyCenter using the state-of-risk field named in the signed mapping.
Re-run the complaint count split between consumer-direct and department-forwarded and compare it to the CDS reconciliation.
Compare each re-derived figure to the submitted blank and mark any element differing by more than 1% as a fail.
testing.done: the settlement buckets, policy counts and complaint splits are independently re-derived and every element over the 1% tolerance is failed.

testing.step: Trace each sampled blank to its submission confirmation and attestation
actions: Open the RDC filing record for each sampled state, line and company and read the confirmation number, submission timestamp and submitting user.
Confirm the confirmation number matches the one recorded on the compliance filing inventory character for character.
Confirm the attestation was completed by an officer, not by the preparer, and that the attestation date is on or before the submission date.
Confirm the filing shows an accepted status and the receiving jurisdiction includes the sampled state, capturing the acceptance screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled blank traces to an RDC confirmation number, an officer attestation dated on or before submission, and a recorded acceptance.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths for every sampled blank
actions: For each sampled blank, identify the applicable statutory due date - 30 April for the property/casualty lines and 30 June for life, annuity, long-term care, health, lender-placed and travel.
Compare the RDC submission timestamp to that date and compute days early or days late.
Check that the internal 15 March extract freeze and 31 March reconciliation cut-offs were actually met, since a missed internal cut-off is the leading indicator of a late filing.
Treat any submission after the statutory due date as a fail regardless of whether the state raised it.
testing.done: days early/late is computed for every sampled blank against its 30 April or 30 June due date, with any late submission failed.

testing.step: Test the exam readiness file against the Chapter 16 data request
actions: Take the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook Chapter 16 standardized data request and tick off each required register against the readiness file: new business, cancellations/non-renewals, claims paid, claims denied, complaints, producer appointments and terminations.
Open three registers and confirm a data dictionary exists naming every column and that the row counts match the quarterly refresh note.

Pick two procedure documents (claims handling and complaint handling) and confirm the version in the file is the one that was actually in force during the period, using the effective and superseded dates.
Time a live retrieval: request one register and one procedure and record the elapsed time against the 10 business day exam expectation.
testing.done: every Chapter 16 register is present with a data dictionary, procedures are period-correct, and a timed retrieval meets the 10 business day standard.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the data year, state, line, blank, data element and the market conduct impact.
Assign a root cause from the defined set: missed participation change, stale source mapping, unfrozen extract, unresolved validation warning, attestation delay, or register gap.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and where a submitted figure was wrong, record whether a restated blank must be refiled in RDC and by when.
Route every restatement and every missed blank to the Head of Compliance for sign-off and to Regulatory Counsel before any notice goes to a state.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, a root cause from the defined set, an owner, a remediation date and, where needed, a refile commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the results against the thresholds: missed or late blanks (zero tolerance), premium reconciliation variance (0.5%), and data element variance (1%).
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references behind each threshold result.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared, mapped or attested none of the sampled blanks, sign the workpaper.

Report the conclusion, open exceptions and any planned MCAS restatement to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the data year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the three threshold results and the committee reporting date, and is filed under the data year.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the corrective action plan for every adopted market conduct and financial examination finding and its closure against the agreed date; escalation to Head of Compliance and the Audit Committee

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Alaska Title 21 examination provisions (AS 21.06.120 examinations, AS 21.06.140 the 30-day window to respond to the verified examination report, AS 21.06.150 adoption of the report by order) read with the order or consent agreement actually served on the company (supporting: Alabama Title 27, Arkansas Insurance Code)

In-scope processes.value: Examination response and remediation - draft report review, factual rebuttal, root cause analysis, corrective action design and delivery, consumer restitution, control re-testing and closure - for every finding, criticism and recommendation in an adopted examination report from any of the 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Findings, owners, agreed due dates, evidence and closure sign-off held as issue records in the GRC platform; underlying fixes land in Guidewire PolicyCenter, Guidewire ClaimCenter and the published procedures; regulator correspondence and reports come through iSite+ and the Division of Insurance

Compliance procedure documented.value: Examination Findings Remediation Procedure - report intake, 30-day rebuttal, finding decomposition, lookback population sizing, root cause analysis, corrective action plan drafting, restitution calculation with interest, evidence pack per finding, independent validation and regulator status reporting

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and General Counsel; refreshed after every adopted examination order and reviewed annually against the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven and unforgiving - written rebuttal to the verified draft report within 30 days of receipt under AS 21.06.140; corrective action plan to the Division within the period the adoption order states (commonly 30 days from the order); per-finding remediation due dates from the order or consent agreement; restitution completion and proof-of-payment report by the date in the order

Deadline reminders configured.value: On report receipt, the GRC platform is loaded with the rebuttal date and every per-finding due date, with alerts to the finding owner and Compliance Manager at T-30, T-14, T-7 and T-1 days and a daily alert once a finding is past due

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Draft and adopted examination reports, the written rebuttal, the adoption order, the corrective action plan, per-finding evidence packs, restitution registers and payment proofs, validation testing workpapers and the closure letter are retained 7 years from finding closure

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A finding closed without validation evidence, a missed agreed remediation date, an under-calculated restitution amount, or a recurrence of a previously closed finding is logged as a remediation exception with root cause, owner and re-opening decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Independent validation and closure sign-off on every finding before it is reported closed to the Division of Insurance; the finding owner cannot close their own finding

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every finding, criticism and recommendation in every examination report adopted in the period across the 51 jurisdictions, plus the underlying remediated transactions - repriced policies, re-adjudicated claims and restitution payments - behind each finding

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero findings closed past the agreed date without a documented, regulator-acknowledged extension; zero findings closed without independent validation evidence; restitution recomputation must agree to the amount paid within USD 1 per claimant with 100% of claimants reached or documented as unlocatable; any recurrence of a closed finding fails outright

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven per adopted report, so testing runs at two points - within 30 days of each finding's claimed closure, and quarterly across all open and closed-in-quarter findings - rather than on an annual cycle

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be outside the remediating function, must not have designed or executed the corrective action, and must not report to the finding owner

Evidence location for test results.value: Per-examination remediation validation workpaper - finding register extract, sample, re-performance notes, restitution recomputation schedule and exception log - filed in the compliance evidence repository under the examination number and state

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Finding-by-finding closure pack keyed to the examination report paragraph numbers - corrective action taken, date implemented, validation evidence, restitution register with payment proofs - producible to the Alaska Division of Insurance or a re-examination team within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Compliance is the single point of contact for the examiner-in-charge and the Division of Insurance on remediation status; Regulatory Counsel clears every rebuttal, extension request and closure representation, and General Counsel approves anything touching a consent order or fine

checklist.step: Take in the verified draft examination report and start the 30-day clock
actions: Log the report the day it arrives: examination number, state, examiner-in-charge, examination period, lines reviewed, date of receipt and the delivery channel (iSite+ message, Division letter or examiner email).
Compute and record the rebuttal deadline as receipt date plus 30 days under AS 21.06.140 and put it on the compliance calendar as a hard date.
Open a parent remediation record in the GRC platform with the examination number as the key and attach the full draft report.
Notify the Head of Compliance, General Counsel and the heads of every function named in the report within one business day of receipt.
Book the rebuttal working sessions inside the 30-day window immediately, because the window does not extend for diary conflicts.
checklist.done: the report is logged with its receipt date, the 30-day rebuttal deadline is calendared, and every named function head has been notified.

checklist.step: Decompose the report into discrete, separately trackable findings
actions: Read the report paragraph by paragraph and create one child record per finding, criticism and recommendation, keyed to the exact report paragraph or standard number.
Copy the examiner's wording verbatim into the record, including the sample size tested, the error count and the error rate the examiner computed.

Classify each record as Finding (statutory violation), Criticism (practice below the Market Regulation Handbook standard) or Recommendation, since only the first two normally carry mandated corrective action.
Tag each record with the process affected (underwriting, rating, claims, complaints, producer licensing, forms) and the statutory cite the examiner relied on.
Never merge two examiner paragraphs into one record - closure is reported paragraph by paragraph.
checklist.done: every report paragraph raising an issue has its own record with verbatim wording, examiner error rate, classification and statutory cite.

checklist.step: Test the factual accuracy of each finding and file the written rebuttal in time
actions: For each finding, pull the specific policy, claim or complaint files the examiner cited and confirm the facts asserted match the file.
Where the examiner's sample was mis-scoped or a file was misread, draft the correction with the file numbers and document images attached as exhibits.
Separate factual disputes from legal disagreements about the statutory interpretation and argue each on its own footing.
Assemble the written submission required by AS 21.06.140 and serve it on the Division of Insurance before the 30th day after receipt, keeping proof of service.
Record for each finding whether the company accepted it, accepted it with clarification, or disputed it, and file the submission with the parent record.
checklist.done: a written rebuttal is served within 30 days of receipt with proof of service, and each finding carries an accepted/clarified/disputed position.

checklist.step: Size the impacted population beyond the examiner's sample
actions: For each accepted finding, define the full population the error condition could have touched - the same product, coverage, rating rule or claims handling path across the whole examination period, not just the examined state.
Query PolicyCenter and ClaimCenter for that population and produce the record count, premium and paid loss exposed, split by state.
Apply the examiner's error condition as a query rule and count the actual affected records, so the company's own error rate can be compared to the examiner's sample rate.
Extend the lookback beyond the examination period where the causing rule or procedure was in force earlier, and state the earliest date the condition could exist.
Hand the sized population to the Compliance Manager and the finding owner - remediation scoped to the examiner's sample alone is the most common repeat-finding cause.
checklist.done: each accepted finding has a sized, dated, multi-state impacted population with the company's own error rate computed against it.

checklist.step: Run root cause analysis to a system, rule or control, not a person
actions: Hold a root cause session with the finding owner and the owning system's Business Systems Analyst and drive the cause to a named artefact: a rating rule, a policy admin configuration, a claims workflow step, a procedure paragraph, or a missing control.
Record whether the cause is design (the rule was wrong) or operation (the rule was right and was not followed), because the corrective action differs completely.
Check the finding register for the same cause in a prior examination in any state; a repeat cause is escalated to the Head of Compliance the same day.
Write the cause statement into the finding record in one sentence naming the artefact and the date it entered service.
Reject cause statements that read as human error alone unless a training or supervision control gap is named alongside it.
checklist.done: every accepted finding carries a one-sentence cause naming a specific artefact, a design/operation classification and a repeat-cause check.

checklist.step: Design the corrective action and agree the delivery date with the regulator
actions: Draft, per finding, the corrective action set: the system or rule change, the procedure rewrite, the training to be delivered, the new monitoring control and the consumer remediation.
Attach a delivery date to each action derived from the release calendar rather than optimism, and name an accountable owner at manager level or above.
Assemble the actions into the corrective action plan document keyed to the report paragraph numbers and have Regulatory Counsel clear it.
Submit the plan to the Alaska Division of Insurance within the period stated in the adoption order under AS 21.06.150 and record the submission date and recipient.
Where the Division negotiates a different date, replace the internal date with the agreed date in the GRC record and note who agreed it and when.
checklist.done: a counsel-cleared corrective action plan keyed to report paragraphs is submitted to the Division and every action carries the agreed date and a named owner.

checklist.step: Compute consumer restitution with interest and build the payee register
actions: For each finding that underpaid a claim or overcharged a premium, compute per consumer the correct amount, the amount actually paid or charged, and the shortfall.
Add interest at the rate the order or state statute specifies, running from the original due date to the planned payment date, and show the rate and day count on each line.
Build the restitution register with claimant/policyholder name, policy or claim number, state, shortfall, interest, total due and last known address.
Have the Controller review the total and confirm the funding and the general ledger account before any payment run.
Flag unlocatable payees for the state unclaimed property process rather than dropping them from the register.
checklist.done: a per-consumer restitution register with shortfall, interest rate, day count and total due exists and the total is confirmed by the Controller.

checklist.step: Load every action into the tracker with owner, agreed date and evidence requirement
actions: Create a tracker task per corrective action under its finding record, carrying the owner, the agreed regulator date, the internal target date and the evidence artefact required at closure.

State the evidence requirement concretely per task - a release note and post-implementation test result for a system change, a version-stamped procedure for a rewrite, an attendance and pass-rate report for training, a payment file for restitution.
Configure the T-30/T-14/T-7/T-1 alerts to the owner and Compliance Manager and a daily alert once past due.
Block the task status from moving to Closed until the named evidence artefact is attached.
Publish an open-findings dashboard to the Head of Compliance weekly showing days to agreed date per finding.
checklist.done: every corrective action is a tracked task with an owner, an agreed date, a named required evidence artefact and closure blocked without it.

checklist.step: Deliver the system, rule and procedure changes
actions: Raise the change request against the named artefact - the rating rule, the eligibility rule, the policy admin configuration or the claims workflow step identified as the cause.
Specify the corrected behaviour in the requirement, including the effective date the change must apply from, and reference the finding paragraph number in the change record.
Test the fix against the examiner's own cited files: re-run those exact policies or claims through the changed rule and confirm they now produce the correct outcome.
Deploy through the normal release process and capture the release note, deployment date and post-implementation test result.
Where the corrected rule requires a rate or form filing, hand the change to the Regulatory Filing Specialist rather than deploying it unfiled.
checklist.done: the causing artefact is changed, retested against the examiner's own cited files, deployed with a dated release note, and filed where filing is required.

checklist.step: Rewrite the procedure and train the affected staff
actions: Rewrite the affected procedure paragraph so it states the required behaviour explicitly, and version-stamp it with the new effective date and the superseded version.
Have the owning function head and the Compliance Manager approve the new version and publish it to the document repository staff actually use.
Build a short training module covering what changed, why the examiner raised it and what the handler must now do, and assign it to every affected handler with a completion deadline.
Pull the completion and pass-rate report and chase non-completers through their manager until the rate reaches 100%.
Attach the published procedure and the completion report to the finding record as closure evidence.
checklist.done: the procedure is republished with effective and superseded dates and training completion reaches 100% of affected staff with the report attached.

checklist.step: Execute the restitution payments and prove they reached the consumers
actions: Release the restitution payment file against the Controller-approved register and record the payment date, method and reference per payee.
Send the explanatory letter the order requires with each payment, stating the examination, the reason for the payment and the interest included, cleared by Regulatory Counsel before the first send.
Track returned mail and uncashed instruments and re-attempt through address verification before treating a payee as unlocatable.
Escheat unlocatable amounts through the state unclaimed property process and keep the escheat filing as evidence.
Produce the proof-of-payment report the order requires and submit it to the Division of Insurance by the date stated.
checklist.done: every register line shows a payment reference or a documented escheat, and the proof-of-payment report is submitted to the Division on time.

checklist.step: Assemble the per-finding closure evidence pack
actions: Build one pack per finding containing the report paragraph, the accepted position, the cause statement, each corrective action with its delivery evidence, and the restitution register extract.
Include the post-implementation test showing the corrected outcome on the examiner's own cited files, since that is what a re-examination team looks for first.
Name the pack <state>-<examination number>-<paragraph number> so it is retrievable exactly the way the regulator refers to the finding.
Index the pack in the compliance evidence repository under the examination and confirm it is retrievable within the 5 business day response standard.
Leave the finding status at Pending Validation - the pack alone does not close it.
checklist.done: each finding has a paragraph-keyed evidence pack including the post-implementation test, indexed and retrievable within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Have the finding independently validated before it is called closed
actions: Take each finding claiming closure and re-test the control on a fresh post-fix population rather than on the records the remediation team already corrected.
Draw at least 25 post-implementation transactions from the affected process and confirm the error condition no longer occurs.
Confirm every corrective action task carries its named evidence artefact and that the artefact actually shows what it claims.
Return findings to the owner where the post-fix sample still shows the error, and record the return date and reason on the finding record.
Only findings passing the post-fix sample move to Validated.
checklist.done: each closed-claim finding passes a fresh post-implementation sample of at least 25 transactions or is returned to its owner with a written reason.

checklist.step: Report status to the Division and close out with the Chief Audit Executive
actions: Review the Validated findings and sign the closure record; a finding owner may not sign their own finding closed.
Approve the status report to the Alaska Division of Insurance keyed to report paragraph numbers, stating for each finding the action taken, the implementation date and the validation result.
Where an agreed date will be missed, approve a written extension request to the examiner-in-charge before the date passes, never after, and record the Division's response.
Present open and overdue findings to the Audit Committee at its next sitting with days overdue and owner named.
Report closure to the Division and retain the acknowledgement or closure letter on the parent examination record.
checklist.done: every closed finding carries an independent closure signature, the paragraph-keyed status report is with the Division, and overdue findings are before the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Retain the examination and remediation record and watch for recurrence
actions: Archive the parent examination record - draft report, rebuttal and proof of service, adoption order, corrective action plan, all finding packs, restitution register and payment proofs, validation workpapers and the closure letter.
Apply the 7-year-from-closure retention label and keep the legal hold in place while any related consent order, fine or consumer litigation is open.
Register each closed finding's cause in the recurring-issue watch list so the next examination in any state is checked against it first.
Schedule a 12-month post-closure re-test of the highest-severity findings and put it on the compliance calendar as a committed task.
Confirm the archive is retrievable by state, examination number and report paragraph number.
checklist.done: the full examination record is archived with 7-year retention, causes are on the recurrence watch list, and a 12-month re-test is calendared.

testing.step: Build the population of findings from the adopted reports themselves
actions: Collect every examination report adopted in the period across the 51 jurisdictions from the compliance correspondence file and the iSite+ message history, not from the tracker.
Read each report and count the findings, criticisms and recommendations paragraph by paragraph, recording the report paragraph number for each.
Record for each the state, examination number, examination period, process affected and the agreed remediation date stated in the order or plan.
Sign the population as complete and note the date and the reports it was built from.
testing.done: a paragraph-level finding population is built directly from the adopted reports and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the report population to the tracker's finding register
actions: Extract every finding record from the GRC platform for the same examinations with its status, owner, agreed date and closure date.
Match tracker records to report paragraphs one to one and list any report paragraph with no tracker record as an automatic exception.
List any tracker record merging two report paragraphs, since merged findings cannot be closed paragraph by paragraph to the regulator.
Confirm the agreed date on each tracker record matches the date in the order or the accepted corrective action plan, character for character.
testing.done: every report paragraph matches exactly one tracker record with an agreed date matching the order, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of findings to re-test
actions: Take 100% of findings classified as statutory violations, 100% of findings involving consumer restitution and 100% of repeat-cause findings.
Take 15 further findings selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining criticisms and recommendations.
Include every finding closed in the period regardless of classification, since closure is the assertion being tested.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all violations, all restitution findings, all repeat causes and all period closures is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the remediation effectiveness test on a fresh post-fix population
actions: For each sampled finding, define the error condition from the examiner's own wording rather than from the company's cause statement.
Draw 25 transactions processed after the recorded implementation date from PolicyCenter or ClaimCenter for the affected process and state.
Apply the error condition and compute the post-fix error rate; compare it to the examiner's original sample error rate.
Any post-fix occurrence of the error condition fails the finding regardless of the closure evidence on file, and the finding is reported as improperly closed.
testing.done: each sampled finding has a post-fix error rate computed on 25 fresh transactions, and any recurrence fails the closure.

testing.step: Recompute the restitution amounts and the interest maths
actions: Select 20 payees from the restitution register across the sampled findings, weighted to the largest amounts.
Recompute the shortfall from the source claim or policy record: correct amount less amount actually paid or charged.
Recompute interest independently using the rate the order or state statute specifies and your own day count from the original due date to the payment date.
Compare your total to the register total per payee and fail any line differing by more than USD 1.
Recompute the register completeness by re-running the impacted-population query yourself and confirming no eligible consumer is missing from the register.
testing.done: 20 recomputed payee lines agree to the register within USD 1 and an independent population re-run finds no missing eligible consumer.

testing.step: Trace restitution payments to proof of receipt or documented escheat
actions: For each of the 20 sampled payees, trace the register line to a payment record with date, method and reference in the payment system.
Confirm the explanatory letter required by the order accompanied the payment by pulling the correspondence record.
For uncashed or returned items, confirm the re-attempt was made and that unlocatable amounts were escheated with a filing reference.
Confirm the proof-of-payment report submitted to the Division reconciles to the register total, and capture the submission acknowledgement.
testing.done: every sampled payee traces to a payment reference or an escheat filing, and the report submitted to the Division reconciles to the register.

testing.step: Recompute the timeliness of the rebuttal and every agreed remediation date
actions: For each sampled examination, recompute the rebuttal deadline as report receipt date plus 30 days under AS 21.06.140 and compare it to the proof-of-service date on the written submission.
For each sampled finding, compute days early or late as closure date minus agreed date from the order or accepted plan.
Confirm every late closure has a written extension requested before the original date passed and a recorded Division response; an extension requested after the date is not an extension.
Compute the on-time closure rate against the zero-tolerance threshold and list every finding closed late without an approved extension.
testing.done: the 30-day rebuttal timing and every finding's days early/late are recomputed, with late closures lacking a pre-dated extension listed.

testing.step: Test the root cause quality and check for recurrence across states
actions: Read each sampled cause statement and confirm it names a specific artefact - rule, configuration, workflow step, procedure paragraph or missing control - and a design/operation classification.
Reject cause statements resting on human error alone with no training or supervision control named.
Search the finding register across all 51 jurisdictions for the same cause in any prior examination and flag every repeat.
For each repeat, check whether the earlier corrective action was validated and why it did not hold, and record that assessment on the finding.
testing.done: every sampled cause names an artefact and a classification, and each cross-state repeat carries a written assessment of why the earlier fix failed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the state, examination number, report paragraph, what failed and the regulatory exposure it creates.

Assign a root cause from the defined set: finding not registered, agreed date mis-recorded, remediation scoped to the examiner's sample only, closed without validation evidence, restitution under-calculated, or recurrence of a closed finding.
Re-open in the GRC platform any finding that was improperly closed and notify the Head of Compliance the same day.
Where a closure was already represented to the Division, route a correction notice through Regulatory Counsel before it is sent, and record the send date.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with a defined root cause, improperly closed findings are re-opened, and any corrective notice to the Division is counsel-cleared.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the results against the thresholds: on-time closure (zero tolerance without a pre-dated extension), validation evidence on 100% of closures, restitution accuracy within USD 1 per payee, and zero recurrences.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper reference behind each threshold result.
Have the independent reviewer, who designed and executed none of the sampled corrective actions and does not report to any finding owner, sign the workpaper.

Report the conclusion, re-opened findings and overdue remediation to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the examination number and state.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the four threshold results and the Audit Committee reporting date, filed under the examination number.
